mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds Rate above 5.25% in a given month leads to a near-term negative S&P 500 20-day forward return as investors anticipate higher borrowing costs eroding growth prospects.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero during the same month (t-test p > 0.05), or FEDFUNDS does not exceed 5.25% in any month during the horizon.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in unemployment claims (PAYEMS) below the prior month's level, accompanied by a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE), signals a strengthening labor market and supports S&P 500 positive 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS < previous PAYEMS AND UNRATE < previous UNRATE
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in > 60% of similar labor-market signal events (rolling IC < -0.1), or unemployment falls are not accompanied by equity gains.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly surge in retail sales (HOUST) exceeding 2% year-over-year growth coincides with a decline in industrial production (INDPRO), indicating a shift from inventory-driven to consumption-driven demand, which predicts a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: HOUST YoY growth > +2% AND INDPRO < previous INDPRO
regime_hint: Transition from supply shock to consumption recovery
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive during 10 such signal events (IC < 0.05), or the consumption shift is not observed in the data.

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive 2-month decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 50-week moving average, without a corresponding drop in consumer demand proxies (HOUST), predicts a negative 5-day S&P 500 forward return as supply constraints worsen.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 50-week MA for 2 consecutive months AND HOUST > 50-week MA
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not negative in >80% of such events (rolling IC > -0.2), or demand recovers in parallel with production.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) over three consecutive months, when the 10-year Treasury yield is flat or falling, predicts a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as deflationary expectations boost equity valuations.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive during 5 such CPI declines (IC < 0.05), or Treasury yields rise during the window.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in job openings (not directly observable in the provided proxies, but as a regime signal) coincides with a decline in unemployment (UNRATE) and a sharp increase in payrolls (PAYEMS), predicting a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return in labor market tightening.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < previous AND PAYEMS > previous AND (regime:job_openings_rising)
regime_hint: Labor market tightening regime (implied by rising job openings)
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in >70% of such labor-market tightening events (rolling IC < -0.15), or payrolls do not increase as expected.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly drop in retail sales (HOUST) of 3% or more, without a concurrent decline in industrial production (INDPRO), signals weak consumption and predicts a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: HOUST < previous by >= -3% AND INDPRO > previous
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative in >50% of such consumption shocks (IC > -0.1), or production declines in parallel.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent 6-month decline in the 10-year Treasury yield below 3.5% signals central bank easing that, when sustained, is associated with a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return via lower discounting of future cash flows.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not statistically positive in >70% of such 6-month yield declines (rolling IC < 0.05), or yield does not remain below 3.5% for the full horizon.
